```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
```

```{r}
data <- read_csv("data/household_data_integrated.csv")
dictionary <- read_csv("data/data_dictionary.csv")
```
```{r}
nrow(data); ncol(data)
```
```{r}
#Problem : Task 3's integration must have produced excatly one row per household. Verifying this will help protect every downstream step.
```

```{r}
#Make sure there is only one row for each household before analysing the data.
nrow(data)
n_distinct(data$HouseholdID)
dup_ids <- data %>%
  count(HouseholdID) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

dup_ids
data %>%
  filter(HouseholdID %in% dup_ids$HouseholdID) %>%
  arrange(HouseholdID)
data <- data %>% distinct()
data <- data %>%
  group_by(HouseholdID) %>%
  slice(1) %>%   # or slice_max(some_date_column), or another rule
  ungroup()
n_distinct(data$HouseholdID) == nrow(data)
```

```{r}
n_distinct(data$HouseholdID) == nrow(data)
```
```{r}
# Problem : Task 3 's integration must have produced excatly one row per household. Verifying this now protects every downstream step.
```

```{r}
sum(is.na(data))
```
```{r}
colSums(is.na(data)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(10)
```
```{r}
## STEP 1: DEFINE THE MODELLING TARGET
data <- data %>% mutate(FoodInsecure_flag = factor(FoodInsecure_flag, levels = c(0,1)))

table(data$FoodInsecure_flag)
prop.table(table(data$FoodInsecure_flag))
#Target: FoodInsecure_flag — 1 means the household ran out of food, and 0 means it did not.
```
```{r}
#Milestone 3 's predictive goal needs a binary modelling target. 
#Treatment : Used FoodInsecure_flag that was alreadu engineered in Task 3 from RanOutOfFoodCode (via RanOutOfFood_label, recoded in Task 2).
```

```{r}
#==============================================================
#Step 2 : Asssesing class imbalance 
#==============================================================

imbalance_ratio <- table(data$FoodInsecure_flag)[1] / table(data$FoodInsecure_flag)[2]
as.numeric(imbalance_ratio)
```
```{r}
#Problem : is the target skewed enough to need resampling? 
#Treatment : check the majority and minority before ratio scaling 
#Verification:ratio ≈ 4.46:1 - moderate, not severe (not 99:1), so addressed through stratified train/ test split in step 7 reather than resampling for example SMOTE 
```

```{r}
# STEP 3: REMOVE IDENTIFIERS 

exclude_tier_vars <- dictionary %>%
  filter(Tier %in% c("Key", "Low")) %>%
  pull(Variable)
exclude_tier_vars

```
```{r}
# Problem identifies and redundant / low-value columns (per the team data dictionary's Tier column) would be meaningless or even misleading as model predictor 
#Treatment : drop every variable that is tagged "Key" or "Low" tier.
```

```{r}
model_data <- data %>% select(-any_of(exclude_tier_vars))

ncol(model_data)
```
```{r}
# STEP 4: REMOVE LEAKAGE VARIABLES
leakage_vars <- c(
  "RanOutOfFoodCode", "RanOutOfFood_label", "RanOutDays", "RanOutDays_clean",
  "HungryButDidNotEatCode", "WholeDayWithoutEatingCode",
  "SkippedMealCode", "SkippedMealDays", "SkippedMealDays_clean",
  "AteLessCode", "AteLessDays", "AteLessDays_clean",
  "WorriedFoodWouldRunOutCode", "UnableToEatHealthyFoodCode",
  "AteFewFoodsCode", "FewFoodsDays", "FewFoodsDays_clean",
  "AdultHungerCode", "ChildHungerCode")
```


```{r}

intersect(leakage_vars, names(model_data))
model_data <- model_data %>% select(-any_of(leakage_vars))
ncol(model_data)
```
```{r}
#Probelm : FoodInsecure_flag is built directly from RanOutOfFoodCode. any variable that is from the same food-security question battery is too directly tied to the target and would leak the answer to the model.
#Treatment: Removed all 18 related food-security variables 
```

```{r}
# STEP 5: TRANSFORMATIONS / ENCODING (category levels before/after)
code_vars <- model_data %>%
  select(ends_with("Code")) %>%
  names()
```

```{r}
# Problem : the category codes are stored as integers , which would make R treat as continous numbers reather than categories . 
#Treatment : convery every *Code column to a factor.
```


```{r}
str(model_data[code_vars[1:3]])
```

```{r}
sapply(model_data[code_vars[1:3]], function(x) length(unique(na.omit(x))))
```
```{r}
model_data <- model_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(code_vars), as.factor))
```

```{r}
#Step 6 SCALING (technique-dependent)
numeric_predictors <- model_data %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  select(-any_of(leakage_vars)) %>%
  names()

numeric_predictors
```
```{r}
model_data_scaled <- model_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(numeric_predictors), ~ as.numeric(scale(.))))
```

```{r}
summary(model_data$Income_per_capita)     
summary(model_data_scaled$Income_per_capita)
```
```{r}
#Problem : K-means uses distance calculations so numeric predictors can vary in scales . thousands vs a 0-5 index) would let income dominate purely due to scale , not real importance. 
#Treatment: standardized the z-score all numeric predictors 
```

```{r}
# STEP 7: TRAIN/TEST SPLIT
set.seed(381)

split_index <- createDataPartition(model_data$FoodInsecure_flag, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- model_data[split_index, ]
test_data  <- model_data[-split_index, ]

nrow(train_data); nrow(test_data)
```
```{r}
prop.table(table(train_data$FoodInsecure_flag))
prop.table(table(test_data$FoodInsecure_flag))
```
```{r}
# Problem : needs to hold unseen data to evaluate Milestone 3 models, without the split accidentally breaking the target's class balance. 
#Treatment: stratified 80/20 split , seed =381 for reproductibility.
```

```{r}
# STEP 8: LEAKAGE PREVENTION CHECK
#Confirm that no leakages variable survived into the final or test data 
any(leakage_vars %in% names(train_data))

length(intersect(split_index, setdiff(seq_len(nrow(model_data)), split_index)))
```

```{r verify_train_test_split}
# Verification : the 0 overlap shows that train and test are fully disjoint.
```

```{r}
# STEP 9: FINAL MISSINGNESS CHECK (after Task 4 changes)
sum(is.na(model_data))
```
```{r}
#Check which variables still have missing values in the modelling data so the group knows when interpreting the model results.For milestone 1 
colSums(is.na(model_data)) %>% sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>% head(10)
```
```{r}
# Problem : confirm wether removing leakage/tier variables changes 
#overall missingness, and what remains for the group to be aware of
```

```{r cars}
# ============================================================
# SAVE FINAL MODELLING-READY DATASETS
# ============================================================
write_csv(train_data, "train_data.csv")
write_csv(test_data, "test_data.csv")
write_csv(model_data, "model_data_full.csv")
write_csv(model_data_scaled, "model_data_scaled.csv")
```
